title: Decoder-specific copy thresholds and endpoint scope
statement: For p in (1/2,1), positive gap g=(1-c)(2p-1)-c is equivalent to c<1-1/(2p), and this threshold lies strictly between zero and one half. At c=1, equal positive replication per lineage and a declared joint product Bernoulli law reduce fair majority to the finite K-vote binomial formula, including half the tie mass.
assumptions: Decoder and tie rule are named
Product law is declared and checked for each finite PMF; pairwise marginals do not substitute
c=1 equal-vote conclusion requires equal lineage replication; unequal weights use their actual weighted decoder
Existing 0.4.6 off-diagonal and conditional diagonal contracts retain all their original assumptions
boundary: The positive-gap algebra is not a kernel proof of a Hoeffding inequality. Uniform concentration needs the joint-law hypotheses and its concentration proof; the complete uniform bound in Lean stays open. Generic optimal blind-decoder limits and monotonicity of the decoder gap remain open.
status: Lean algebraic boundary, finite endpoint PMFs and explicit inventory; no replacement of published probability theorems
runtimeAPI: No new runtime export; these contracts and their native finite witnesses extend the admitted theory without duplicating the engine.
